story: Alex meticulously folded the laundry, each shirt smoothed with unnecessary force, the corners sharp enough to cut. The chipped ceramic mug warmed their hands, but did little for the chill that had settled deep in their chest. They stared at the garden, at how the neighbor’s roses bloomed so effortlessly while their own seedlings remained stubbornly green. Alex abruptly stood, leaving the neatly stacked clothes, and walked to the shed, grabbing the heaviest gardening tool. The soil felt strangely…resistant under the shovel’s blade, and they drove it in with a force that vibrated up their arms.

Alex meticulously folded the laundry, each shirt smoothed with excessive pressure, the corners precise enough to cut skin. The chipped ceramic mug warmed his hands, but didn’t seem to penetrate the chill that had settled deep in his chest. He’d offered to help with dinner, genuinely, but was met with a dismissive wave and a pointed remark about his “lack of kitchen sense.” Alex’s jaw tightened, and he gripped the mug harder, feeling the heat become almost painful. He carried the folded clothes upstairs, placing them in neat stacks, deliberately avoiding eye contact with anyone he passed, a silent retreat into order.

Alex stared at the chipped ceramic mug, the lukewarm tea doing nothing to settle the tightness in his chest. He’d spent the last three hours meticulously building the birdhouse, following the plans his grandfather had sketched years ago, only to have it dismissed with a careless wave of the hand. His knuckles were white where he gripped the mug, and a pulse throbbed visibly in his jaw. He abruptly stood, scraping the chair against the kitchen floor, the sound unnecessarily loud in the quiet room. Alex carried the birdhouse to the shed, the wood feeling heavy and wrong in his hands, and set it down amongst the forgotten tools.
